tariq: Heads-up: after the midnight firmware push in us-west-2 we started seeing MIG slice rebinds and sudden slab fragmentation on machines in rack-22. A handful of dedicated slices reported 95/99 spikes. anyone on-call?

lin: looking. I see a pattern: host agent reported 'bind_mismatch' events and then kube-proxy churned for the gpuslice controller. log excerpt: `gpu-agent: detected MIG-id mismatch, issuing rebind -> node k8s-binding-update`.

frank: Are these new physical firmware changes or driver roll-forward? The change set was the vendor micro-patch (fw v3.2.1) that landed 02:11. Might be altering device enumeration order.

devops-bot: [NOTICE] fw-rollout/us-west-2 completed 2026-02-10T02:15:00Z -> affected-nodes=14 -> remediation-suggested=[quiesce-allocs, rebind-cleanup, temporary-routing]

lin: confirmed. Device enumeration shifted on 6 nodes in rack-22 which caused the MIG-ID mapping to change; allocator then attempted to reconcile and created short-lived vacuums that triggered KV cache spills and small-allocation storms.

sara: net effect: dedicated-slices got noisy because allocator temporarily overpacked other tenants into leftover slots. We're seeing 20-40% increased tail latency for dedicated workloads in that rack.

frank: proposal: run a targeted rebind-cleanup script that stabilizes MIG mapping without full node reboot: `/infra gpu-util rebind-fix --node node-22-{01..06} --safe`. This should avoid extra preemptions.

lin: +1 but we should also apply a routing policy shim to avoid placing new dedicated allocations on rack-22 for ~45m:```routing.set --scope region:us-west-2 --avoid rack-22 --duration 45m --reason 'fw-enum-rebind'```

tariq: agree. Also set bind_fallback to true for the allocator on affected racks so that if mapping fails we fall back to per-tenant soft-isolation instead of reassigning other tenants into ded slices:```kubectl -n infra set env allocator BIND_FALLBACK=true --context us-west-2```

platform-bot: [ACTION] created incident INC-2026-0210-09: title='MIG rebind after firmware -> dedicated tail spikes' assigned=[infra, allocator] severity=sev2

sara: approx cost impact if we carve fractional-dedicated for affected tenants: extra GPUs ~ 3 for 45m -> est $18. we should log in incident cost tracker.

frank: running rebind-fix as canary on node-22-01 now. watching agent logs. will roll if clean.

lin: adding quick check to scheduler to halt any shuffle reconciles for 10m:```/infra scheduler-config patch --name avoid-shuffle --values '{"reconcile_backoff_ms":600000}'``` this prevents cascading reassignments during the fix window.

devops-bot: [ALERT] node-22-01 rebind-fix succeeded 2026-02-10T02:28:10Z -> migration-minutes=1 -> agent_events=[bind_fix, kv_flush].

frank: node-22-01 looks clean, tail back to baseline. proceeding to node-22-02 then monitor.

tariq: after 3 nodes done we should lift the avoid-rack shim gradually. don't fully open until all nodes green. also add a short-term metric alert for 'dedicated_slice_reassign_rate' > 5/min.

sara: opened a revert MR to hold fw v3.2.1 in canary until we confirm vendor fix. MR: https://git.redwood/infra/fw-hold/mr/12345

lin: follow-up items: 1) add unit test that simulates device-enumeration drift for allocator, 2) create an eval load with MIG-heavy prompt switching, 3) update runbook with the `rebind-fix` command.

platform-bot: [COMMENT] remind: if we choose to quarantine tenants into fractional-dedicated slices, estimate incremental cost and tag customer teams for communication.

tariq: noting cost and comms. tracking on INC-2026-0210-09 -> will draft email for impacted customers after calmer state.

frank: rolling through nodes 02-04 now, progress looks good. will report back in 20m. :+1:
